\chapter{Background}
\label{ch:background}

\section{Replicated documents}
Each client holds a full copy of the document and applies local edits at
once. Edits travel as small updates that commute, so every replica reaches the
same state no matter the order in which updates arrive \cite{shapiro11}.

Figure~\ref{fig:architecture} shows the parts involved. The relay server sits
between the clients and the storage layer.

\section{Cost model}
Let $r$ be the number of reads and $w$ the number of writes per minute. With
a hit rate $h$, the expected storage cost per minute is
\begin{equation}
  C = (1 - h)\, r\, c_r + w\, c_w ,
  \label{eq:cost}
\end{equation}
where $c_r$ and $c_w$ are the costs of one read and one write. Knuth's advice
on premature optimisation \cite{knuth74} applies: measure before tuning.
